- Overestimate prices after recent spikes or positive sentiment; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment remains below -0.30 for 3+ consecutive days.
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 3–5 day delays) are consistently overpredicted; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive, model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at 1.5x recent high if sentiment > 0.30 for 2+ days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; if sentiment flips within 2 days, reduce forecast volatility by 30–50% unless confirmed by price action.
